record.paper_title: Course 6 - Short-Range Spin Glasses: Selected Open Problems
record.original_question: For finite-dimensional Edwards-Anderson short-range Ising spin glass models, where Ising spins take values +1 or -1 on lattice sites and interact through random nearest-neighbor couplings, does a thermodynamic phase transition to a low-temperature spin glass phase occur? Can the Fortuin-Kasteleyn random cluster representation be used to give a rigorous proof of such a phase transition?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Edwards–Anderson short-range Ising spin glass on the d-dimensional integer lattice Z^d (d ≥ 2). To each site x ∈ Z^d assign an Ising spin σ_x ∈ {+1,−1}, and to each nearest-neighbor edge {x,y} of Z^d assign an independent random coupling J_{xy}, drawn from a common symmetric distribution (e.g. standard Gaussian, or symmetric Bernoulli ±1). For a finite box Λ ⊂ Z^d with boundary condition, define the Hamiltonian

  H_Λ(σ) = − Σ_{{x,y}⊂Λ, |x−y|=1} J_{xy} σ_x σ_y,

and the corresponding finite-volume Gibbs measure at inverse temperature β ≥ 0 with partition function Z_Λ(β). Take any thermodynamic-limit infinite-volume Gibbs state obtained from this finite-volume specification.

(a) Does there exist a dimension d and an inverse temperature 0 < β_c < ∞ such that, almost surely with respect to the disorder, the system exhibits a thermodynamic phase transition at β_c — for instance, in the sense that the quenched free energy is non-analytic at β_c, or that the Edwards–Anderson order parameter
  q_EA = lim_{|x−y|→∞} E[ ⟨σ_x σ_y⟩_β^2 ]
vanishes for β < β_c and is strictly positive for β > β_c?

(b) Can a Fortuin–Kasteleyn-type random-cluster representation of the Edwards–Anderson model be developed and used to give a rigorous proof of such a phase transition, in analogy with the FK-representation proof of the phase transition in the ferromagnetic Ising model?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a finite-temperature spin glass phase transition in the finite-dimensional Edwards–Anderson model remains a major open problem in mathematical physics, with no rigorous proof known in any dimension d ≥ 2 and no widely accepted precise conjecture. Recent work by Chatterjee (2023) established rigorous glassy behavior of the ground state at zero temperature in all dimensions, but did not resolve the positive-temperature phase transition. No rigorous Fortuin–Kasteleyn-type proof of an EA phase transition is known.

status_evidence.title: Spin glass phase at zero temperature in the Edwards-Anderson model
status_evidence.snippet: First mathematical proof of glassy behavior in a short-range spin glass model, at zero temperature; the question of a positive-temperature phase transition is described as open.
status_evidence.claim: Positive-temperature phase transition for EA model is open; only zero-temperature glassy behavior has been rigorously established.

status_evidence.title: Spin glass phase at zero temperature in the Edwards–Anderson model (HTML)
status_evidence.snippet: Regarding phase transitions at nonzero temperature, the most basic open question is whether the system has any kind of phase transition in any dimension, with no rigorous result known and no precise conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No rigorous result is known for any nonzero-temperature phase transition in the EA model.
